guarantees.claim: keymgr_key[0] is driven as the bitwise XOR of all keymgr_key_i.key shares (index 0 to Shares-1), after being initialized to zero.

assumptions.claim: keymgr_key_i.key must provide at least Shares elements, each exactly KeyMgrKeyW bits wide, to match the loop bound and bit-slice used in XOR.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds array access or width mismatch leads to undefined key value, potentially exposing or corrupting secret material.

uncertain_points.claim: The XOR-based unmasking of key shares is performed combinational; this may produce glitchy intermediate values that leak secret key bits through power or EM side channels.
uncertain_points.risk: Secret key material could be recovered via side-channel analysis if no additional countermeasures (e.g., register re-timing, masked logic) are present.

uncertain_points.claim: Only keymgr_key[0] is computed; the purpose and usage of other potential indices of keymgr_key (if it is a multi-element array) are not visible in this chunk.
uncertain_points.risk: Incomplete key reconstruction or misrouting of unmasked key value might cause incorrect operation or expose key material to unintended destinations.

uncertain_points.claim: The loop uses keymgr_pkg::Shares and the bit-slice width KeyMgrKeyW without local assertions; if these parameters disagree with the actual dimensions of keymgr_key_i.key, the XOR result will be silently wrong.
uncertain_points.cond: if keymgr_pkg::Shares != actual number of keymgr_key_i.key elements or KeyMgrKeyW != actual bit width
uncertain_points.risk: A mismatched parameter configuration produces an incorrect key value, potentially granting access or breaking security protocols.
